One of the most successful ways to combat noise is to develop quieter aircraft engines and that goal is constantly before both the airlines and the manufacturers.

﻿THE STORY IN THE PACIFIC
On November 22, 1935 a flying boat christened "China Clipper" rose from the waters of San Francisco Bay and headed westward for Manila on the first trans-Pacific air mail flight in history. Twenty-one hours later the Clipper made its first landfall at Honolulu. On the 2400-mile flight it had maintained an average speed of 115 miles per hour.
On February 8, 1954, another Clipper--this one named "Queen of the Pacific"—took^ off from Tokyo, climbed 25,000 feet into an upper air phenomenon known as the jet stream. "Riding" this tremendous river of high-velocity wind, the Clipper roared from Japan to the Hawaiian Islands in 9 hours 18 minutes.
